page_placements.theme: Refinements and look-alikes of the copy-suppression mechanism

record.tranche_reason: Tests copy-suppression-like structures and their function in a newly trained one-layer list-sorting transformer, a different setting from GPT-2 small.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on copy-suppression circuits, head ablations, confidence, and specialization across some toy-model settings. The 76.9% figure is cited from prior work, not measured here. It does not test GPT-2 small L10H7 or ordinary text.
record.test_reason: The study trains one-layer attention-only list-sorting transformers and finds heads it explicitly relates to GPT-2 copy suppression. It tests whether they are the same circuit structure (V5) and whether their functional role is calibration (V3), using OV/QK inspection, mean-ablation and entropy. It does not study GPT-2 small, L10H7, loss attribution or self-repair.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that their toy copy-suppressing head slightly adjusts the dominant copying head and increases confidence, unlike the overconfidence reduction proposed for GPT-2. They attribute this to 100% accuracy and propose copy suppression broadly calibrates predictions according to accuracy. They also conclude it emerges at intermediate gap variance, between vocabulary-splitting and 1-head sorting, and caution that the parallel-head architecture differs from GPT-2.
record.recipe_differences: A trained one-layer attention-only list-sorting transformer is analyzed with OV/QK circuits and head ablations; this is not GPT-2 small or the original GPT-2 study's analysis of L10H7.
record.method_sensitivity: Copy-suppression emergence depends on the training-data gap distribution, including its mean and variance; the reported specialization also changes across training stages and head counts.

fits_no_version.finding: On perturbed data (and 3-element lists), the OV circuits look like copying plus copy suppression but the QK circuits differ; the authors call this a different specialization mode.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Copy/suppress-like OV patterns can arise with distinct QK organization that is not the same copy-suppression mechanism.

fits_no_version.finding: Whether copy suppression, vocabulary-splitting or 1-head sorting emerges depends on the mean and variance of gaps between sorted list elements. Copy suppression appears at intermediate variance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In toy sorting transformers, copy-suppression heads emerge from training-data statistics as an intermediate between using and switching off a superfluous head.

record.problems: The evidence is from a toy list-sorting transformer, and the authors caution against generalizing to larger transformers. Circuit-function interpretation is described as approximate. The functional ablation result is reported qualitatively, with no loss-effect percentage or direct calibration metric.
record.rows_left_out: Other dataset and architecture sweeps report specialization types but are not included as separate rows because they do not report additional functional or circuit tests of copy suppression. The 76.9% result is cited from prior work and is not a result of this study.

untested.parts: All: GPT-2 small L10H7 on ordinary text across the training distribution.
All: L10H7's QK/OV circuits and the share of its loss effect they explain (76.9%).
GPT-2 small; whether copy suppression reduces overconfidence when naive copying is wrong; any direct calibration metric.
All: no upstream-copier ablation or self-repair test; the heads run in parallel.
Negative name movers in IOI and other pretrained language models and sizes.
All: no comparison of self-repair sources.

missing.what: Table 2 fixed-δ datasets δ∈[2,12] to [2,19] (variance 7.6–10.5) also end in copy suppression. Lower variance gives 1-head sorting and higher gives vocabulary-splitting.
Further training the Fig. 3 copy-suppression model on Dδ≈4.7 does not move it away from this mode (it is stable).
The authors argue the parallel placement of the heads (no view of the copier's output) and the absence of an MLP are important differences from GPT-2 copy suppression.

record.verdict_notes: The system is a toy one-layer attention-only model, not GPT-2. Rows were relinked from V2 to V5, since nothing tests L10H7's circuits or loss share. All functional results are qualitative, with no numeric loss or entropy values.

versions.untested_parts: GPT-2 small L10H7, ordinary text, and whether this role is main across the training distribution.
The paper studies OV/QK circuits and ablation effects in its toy model, but does not measure what share of loss is explained or test the 76.9% figure.
It measures confidence-related effects in a 100%-accuracy toy model, not calibration across GPT-2 small or whether the model is overconfident when copying is wrong.
No test of self-repair after ablating an upstream copier; the heads in this model work in parallel.
The paper tests analogous structures in a toy list-sorting model and variations of it, not negative name movers in IOI or external models and sizes.
No distribution-wide comparison of copy suppression with LayerNorm rescaling or other self-repair mechanisms.
